title: shred-audit
description: Per-provider shred delivery. provider_stats and audit_counters hold per-interval DELTAS, so panels aggregate over the selected range rather than reading a running total. Top row is absolute and works with a single provider; the row below it is relative and needs two.

target.rawSql:
SELECT started_at AS time,
       'collector ' || tool_version || ' @ ' || git_commit AS text,
       'restart' AS tags
FROM audit_runs
WHERE host = '$host' AND $__timeFilter(started_at)

list.name: host
list.label: capture host
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT host FROM provider_stats ORDER BY 1
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT host FROM provider_stats ORDER BY 1

list.name: source
list.label: gRPC source (filter audit)
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM filter_windows WHERE host = '$host' ORDER BY 1
list.definition: SELECT DISTINCT source FROM filter_windows WHERE host = '$host' ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Health summary — what was tested and how much of it failed
panels.description:
One row per check over the selected time range.

• in range — all data of that unit in the range (shreds received, shreds expected, slots produced ≈ one per 400 ms, getBlock calls).
• tested — how much of it was actually checked; tested % = tested / in range.
• errors / error % — failures among what was tested.

1. Shreds: every UDP shred is checked against the leader's signature (shreds whose slot leader is unknown are not tested); 'not forged' fails on a real signature mismatch, 'Merkle proof present' fails when a relay zeroed the proof; 'delivered' compares each provider's FEC sets with what the leader produced.
2. Deshred: transactions this tool rebuilt from each shred provider's shreds, compared signature-by-signature with getBlock on sampled slots; error % is missed + corrupted + duplicated transactions over the block's transactions.
3. gRPC feeds: non-rotating deshred feeds are checked like 2; rotating feeds are checked per filter by the filter audit instead.
4. RPC: every getBlock behind 2 and 3. A low tested % in 2 or 3 with errors here means the RPC is the bottleneck.

With a Shyft RPC, getBlock carries no votes, so 2 and 3 compare non-vote transactions only.

targets.rawSql:
WITH
slots AS (SELECT GREATEST(($__unixEpochTo() - $__unixEpochFrom()) / 0.4, 1)::bigint AS n),
counters AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE name = 'shreds_parsed'), 0) AS parsed,
         COALESCE(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE name = 'shreds_no_leader'), 0) AS no_leader,
         COALESCE(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE name = 'shreds_sig_bad'), 0) AS sig_bad,
         COALESCE(SUM(value) FILTER (WHERE name = 'shreds_proof_stripped'), 0) AS stripped
  FROM audit_counters WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'),
delivery AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(shreds_data + shreds_code + missed), 0) AS expected,
         COALESCE(SUM(missed), 0) AS missed
  FROM provider_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'),
onchain_rows AS (
  SELECT source, kind, onchain_txns, onchain_bad, onchain_slots_checked,
         onchain_txns - LAG(onchain_txns) OVER w AS d_txns,
         onchain_bad - LAG(onchain_bad) OVER w AS d_bad,
         onchain_slots_checked - LAG(onchain_slots_checked) OVER w AS d_slots
  FROM txn_source_stats WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY ts)),
onchain_by_source AS (
  SELECT source, kind,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d_txns < 0 THEN onchain_txns ELSE COALESCE(d_txns, 0) END) AS txns,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d_bad < 0 THEN onchain_bad ELSE COALESCE(d_bad, 0) END) AS bad,
         SUM(CASE WHEN d_slots < 0 THEN onchain_slots_checked ELSE COALESCE(d_slots, 0) END) AS slots
  FROM onchain_rows GROUP BY source, kind),
onchain AS (
  SELECT k.kind, COALESCE(SUM(o.txns), 0) AS txns, COALESCE(SUM(o.bad), 0) AS bad,
         COALESCE(MAX(o.slots), 0) AS slots
  FROM (VALUES ('shreds'), ('grpc-deshred')) AS k(kind)
  LEFT JOIN onchain_by_source o ON o.kind = k.kind
  GROUP BY k.kind),
filters AS (
  SELECT COALESCE(SUM(expected), 0) AS expected,
         COALESCE(SUM(missed + extra_in_block), 0) AS errors,
         COALESCE(MAX(slots), 0) AS slots
  FROM (SELECT source, SUM(expected) AS expected, SUM(missed) AS missed,
               SUM(extra_in_block) AS extra_in_block, SUM(slots_checked) AS slots
        FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host'
        GROUP BY source) per_source),
rpc AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS calls, COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE status <> 'ok') AS failed
  FROM rpc_block_fetches WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host')
SELECT area, "check", unit, "in range", tested,
       100.0 * tested / NULLIF("in range", 0) AS "tested %",
       errors, 100.0 * errors / NULLIF(error_base, 0) AS "error %"
FROM (
  SELECT 1 AS ord, '1. Shreds (raw UDP)' AS area, 'signature valid — not forged' AS "check", 'shreds' AS unit,
         parsed AS "in range", parsed - no_leader AS tested, sig_bad AS errors, parsed - no_leader AS error_base
  FROM counters
  UNION ALL SELECT 2, '1. Shreds (raw UDP)', 'Merkle proof present — not stripped', 'shreds',
         parsed, parsed - no_leader, stripped, parsed - no_leader FROM counters
  UNION ALL SELECT 3, '1. Shreds (raw UDP)', 'delivered — not missed', 'shreds',
         expected, expected, missed, expected FROM delivery
  UNION ALL SELECT 4, '2. Deshred (txs rebuilt from shreds)', 'match the confirmed block (onchain audit)', 'slots',
         slots.n, onchain.slots, onchain.bad, onchain.txns FROM onchain, slots WHERE onchain.kind = 'shreds'
  UNION ALL SELECT 5, '3. gRPC feeds', 'deshred feed matches the block (onchain audit)', 'slots',
         slots.n, onchain.slots, onchain.bad, onchain.txns FROM onchain, slots WHERE onchain.kind = 'grpc-deshred'
  UNION ALL SELECT 6, '3. gRPC feeds', 'filtered deliveries match the block (filter audit)', 'slots',
         slots.n, filters.slots, filters.errors, filters.expected FROM filters, slots
  UNION ALL SELECT 7, '4. RPC', 'getBlock calls succeeded', 'calls',
         calls, calls, failed, calls FROM rpc
) summary ORDER BY ord

panels.title: Transaction versions — share over time
panels.description: Every distinct transaction this tool rebuilt from the shred providers' shreds, counted once by message version (votes split out of legacy). Stacked to 100%: each band is that version's share at that time. Transactions only seen on a gRPC feed are not counted: the Yellowstone protobuf cannot tell v1 from v0.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       CASE name
         WHEN 'txs_vote' THEN 'legacy — vote'
         WHEN 'txs_legacy' THEN 'legacy — non-vote'
         WHEN 'txs_v0' THEN 'v0'
         WHEN 'txs_v1' THEN 'v1'
       END AS metric,
       value::float AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('txs_vote', 'txs_legacy', 'txs_v0', 'txs_v1')
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Transaction versions — over the range
panels.description: Total distinct transactions per message version over the selected range, with each version's share.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       CASE name
         WHEN 'txs_vote' THEN 'legacy — vote'
         WHEN 'txs_legacy' THEN 'legacy — non-vote'
         WHEN 'txs_v0' THEN 'v0'
         WHEN 'txs_v1' THEN 'v1'
       END AS metric,
       value::float AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('txs_vote', 'txs_legacy', 'txs_v0', 'txs_v1')
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Clean set rate — every shred in the set verified
panels.description:
A set counts as clean only when EVERY shred in it verified, none lacked a known leader, and enough arrived to reconstruct it (agg.rs: `invalid == 0 && unverifiable == 0 && decode_ns.is_some()`). Missed shreds do NOT count against it — Reed-Solomon rebuilds a set from any k of k+m.

It is an all-or-nothing gate over ~60 shreds, so it AMPLIFIES a small per-shred failure rate: at 1% per shred barely half the sets come out clean. Never read this as 'half the data is garbage'. Read the per-shred panel beside it first — that is the honest rate, and this one is its 60th power.

No threshold line: we have no baseline yet. Set one once a week of normal traffic says what normal is.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       sets_valid::float / NULLIF(sets_present, 0) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Per-shred failure rates — the honest number
panels.description:
What the previous panel is made of, without the ~60x per-set amplification.

'invalid' is shreds that failed verification, over shreds delivered. 'no leader' is shreds we could not check at all because the slot's leader was unknown — if that is non-zero the invalid rate is understated and the leader schedule is the thing to fix. 'missed' is over shreds EXPECTED (delivered + missed), so it is comparable between providers regardless of how much traffic each carried.

Providers that delivered nothing are excluded on purpose: a silent feed would otherwise draw a flat 0% and read as the cleanest one on the board.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · invalid' AS metric,
       invalid::float / (shreds_data + shreds_code) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND shreds_data + shreds_code > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · no leader' AS metric,
       sig_unverifiable::float / (shreds_data + shreds_code) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND shreds_data + shreds_code > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · missed' AS metric,
       missed::float / (missed + shreds_data + shreds_code) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND shreds_data + shreds_code > 0
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Set fill time — how long THIS provider took
panels.description: From a provider's first accepted shred of a set to the one that made the set decodable. The only ABSOLUTE latency here: winrate and 'behind fastest' are relative, so a change that slows every provider equally moves neither of them and moves this one. Needs no second provider. 'worst' is the slowest single set in the interval — an intermittent stall barely shifts the mean and spikes there.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · mean' AS metric,
       fill_sum_us / NULLIF(fill_n, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · worst' AS metric,
       fill_max_us AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Winrate — share of contested FEC sets decoded first
panels.description: A set is contested only when two or more providers delivered it validly; delivering alone is not a win. Ties count as a win for each. Empty with a single provider — see the panel's no-data text.

defaults.noValue: no contested sets in this range — a race needs TWO providers delivering the same FEC set validly. With one provider this is empty by definition, not broken. The absolute panels above still work.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       wins::float / races * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND races > 0
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Winner share per source
panels.description: Share of first-delivery (unique) shreds by source. Sums to 100%.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       wins::float / NULLIF(sum(wins) over(partition by ts), 0) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Behind the fastest provider
panels.description: Microseconds behind whoever decoded each contested set first. Mean is SUM(behind_sum_us)/SUM(behind_n) — the table stores the sum unreduced so any range divides exactly, instead of averaging pre-averaged intervals. Run the old and new forwarder side by side as two providers and this panel is the migration verdict.

defaults.noValue: no contested sets in this range — a race needs TWO providers delivering the same FEC set validly. With one provider this is empty by definition, not broken. The absolute panels above still work.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · mean' AS metric,
       behind_sum_us / behind_n AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND behind_n > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · worst' AS metric,
       behind_max_us AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND behind_n > 0
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Coverage — sets this provider turned up for
panels.description: sets_present / sets_total, where the denominator is every distinct set ANY provider delivered this interval. Presence only, valid or not. With a single provider it is 100% by construction — read it next to the usable set rate at the top, never on its own.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       sets_present::float / NULLIF(sets_total, 0) * 100 AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: FEC sets per second
panels.description: Delivery rate per provider, divided by the row's own window_secs so a short first interval or a stalled loop does not distort it.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       sets_present / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Missed shreds per second
panels.description: Shreds a provider never delivered for sets it was part of. Check host health below FIRST: datagrams the kernel dropped from our own socket are absent from the data and inflate this for whoever sent them.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider AS metric,
       missed / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Failed verification, and repeats
panels.description: 'bad data' is block content the leader never signed — treat as substitution until proven otherwise. 'bad proof' is the leader's genuine data whose merkle proof does not reconstruct the signed root: authentic content, unusable shred. 'unclassified' means no provider delivered a leader-authenticated copy to compare against, so it could not be split — with ONE provider everything lands here and the other two read zero. 'repeats' is the same shred delivered twice.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · bad data' AS metric, invalid_data AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · bad proof' AS metric, invalid_sig AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · unclassified' AS metric, invalid_unknown AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time, provider || ' · repeats' AS metric, duplicated AS value FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Stream integrity — is the wire format still what we expect
panels.description: Per second. shreds_after_window is the REORDERING canary: shreds arriving for FEC sets already finalized, which is what a forwarder that buffers or reorders produces. malformed / no_merkle_root mean packets are being mangled; wrong_version means a different cluster or shred version is being relayed; unsupported_variant means something arrived this build cannot parse. All four are zero on a healthy feed.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       name AS metric,
       value::float / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('shreds_after_window', 'shreds_malformed', 'shreds_wrong_version',
               'shreds_unsupported_variant', 'shreds_no_merkle_root', 'shreds_no_leader')
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Data vs coding shreds per second
panels.description: A forwarder that stops relaying CODING shreds looks alive on every other counter — sets keep arriving, they just stop being recoverable from partial delivery. Nothing else here separates the two, so watch the ratio, not the absolute level.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · data' AS metric,
       shreds_data / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
UNION ALL
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' · coding' AS metric,
       shreds_code / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM provider_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Host health — OUR losses, not a provider's
panels.description: Every series here is this machine failing to keep up, not a provider failing to send. udp_kernel_dropped is our socket queue overflowing (raise net.core.rmem_max); udp_channel_full is verification falling behind. Both make the missed-shreds panel look worse than the network was. Non-zero here invalidates a comparison.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       name AS metric,
       value::float / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('udp_kernel_dropped', 'udp_channel_full', 'udp_truncated',
               'udp_no_timestamp', 'udp_unmatched')
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Throughput
panels.description: Datagrams received, shreds parsed out of them, and shreds that failed signature verification — per second.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       name AS metric,
       value::float / NULLIF(window_secs, 0) AS value
FROM audit_counters
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
  AND name IN ('udp_received', 'shreds_parsed', 'shreds_sig_bad', 'shreds_proof_stripped')
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Provider RTT (ICMP)
panels.description: A GAUGE, re-sampled by the pinger on its own timer — consecutive points can repeat one measurement. A coarse network-distance hint, NOT comparable to the decode deltas: ICMP travels a different path and is routinely deprioritised. Use it to EXPLAIN a latency difference, never to measure one. Null = no reply.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time,
       provider || ' ' || ip AS metric,
       rtt_ms AS value
FROM provider_pings
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY ts

panels.title: Transaction deliveries per second — when a feed went quiet
panels.description: txn_source_stats is cumulative, so consecutive rows are differenced here to get a rate. A restart resets the counters, which would read as a large negative rate; those points are dropped so the line breaks instead of diving. The table below says a feed fell behind — this says when.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time,
       metric,
       CASE WHEN d >= 0 THEN d / NULLIF(dt, 0) END AS value
FROM (
  SELECT ts     AS time,
         source AS metric,
         seen - LAG(seen) OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY ts) AS d,
         EXTRACT(epoch FROM ts - LAG(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY source ORDER BY ts)) AS dt
  FROM txn_source_stats
  WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
) s
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Transaction sources — CUMULATIVE for the run
panels.description: The one cumulative table: percentiles come from a histogram spanning the whole process, so this is the latest row per source, not an interval, and it resets when the collector restarts. Do not SUM these columns. onchain bad % is a SAMPLED audit against getBlock — compare sources on the percentage, never on raw counts, and remember pre-execution feeds legitimately carry transactions that never landed. missed / corrupted / duplicated are its three components and are NOT interchangeable: never delivering a transaction is a different accusation from delivering it altered, and only the raw counts tell them apart.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT DISTINCT ON (source)
       source,
       kind,
       seen,
       contested,
       winrate * 100        AS "win %",
       behind_p50_us       AS "p50 µs",
       behind_p90_us       AS "p90 µs",
       behind_p99_us       AS "p99 µs",
       onchain_missed      AS "missed",
       onchain_corrupted   AS "corrupted",
       onchain_duplicated  AS "duplicated",
       onchain_bad_pct * 100 AS "onchain bad %"
FROM txn_source_stats
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
ORDER BY source, ts DESC

panels.title: Filter audit — Correctness — every value here should be 0 or near it
Filter false positives
panels.description: Delivered with a filter's tag, in the confirmed block, but the filter rejects it (filter_slot_checks.extra_in_block). A server-side filter bug. Must be 0.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(extra_in_block),0) AS value FROM filter_slot_checks WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)

panels.title: Tag errors (self-check)
panels.description: Checked on EVERY delivery, not sampled: a tag on a transaction the filter rejects, or a matching transaction delivered without its tag (filter_windows.tag_false_positive + tag_missing). Must be 0.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(tag_false_positive + tag_missing),0) AS value FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)

panels.title: Missed rate
panels.description: Block transactions a filter accepts that were not delivered with its tag, over all sampled slots in range.

targets.rawSql: SELECT SUM(missed)::float / NULLIF(SUM(expected),0) * 100 AS value FROM filter_slot_checks WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)

panels.title: Slots checked
panels.description: Sampled slots compared against getBlock in range (all sources). Flat means the audit is not running — see RPC health.

targets.rawSql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT (source, slot)) AS value FROM filter_slot_checks WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND block_status = 'ok'

panels.title: Missed rate per filter
panels.description: SUM(missed)/SUM(expected) per 5 minutes. A filter that runs intermittently (rotation) shows gaps between its windows — that is expected.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, '5m'), source || ' / ' || filter AS metric,
       SUM(missed)::float / NULLIF(SUM(expected),0) * 100 AS value
FROM filter_slot_checks
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Filter false positives per filter
panels.description: extra_in_block per 5 minutes. Must be 0; anything here is a server filter bug — see the violations table for signatures and the failing clause.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, '5m'), source || ' / ' || filter AS metric, SUM(extra_in_block) AS value
FROM filter_slot_checks
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
GROUP BY 1, 2 HAVING SUM(extra_in_block) > 0 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Not in the confirmed block (forks / phantoms)
panels.description: Delivered, but absent from the confirmed block (extra_not_in_block), as a share of deliveries. Pre-execution feeds carry some transactions from forks that lost, so a low steady rate is normal; a jump is not. Skipped slots count here too.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, '5m'), source AS metric,
       SUM(extra_not_in_block)::float / NULLIF(SUM(delivered),0) * 100 AS value
FROM filter_slot_checks
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Self-check per window
panels.description: Counted on every delivery of every window: tag false positives, missing tags, the server's is_vote disagreeing with the simple-vote rule, and repeat deliveries. Points are per window (at its end).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ended_at AS time, source || ' tag_fp' AS metric, tag_false_positive AS value FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND tag_false_positive > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ended_at, source || ' tag_missing', tag_missing FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND tag_missing > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ended_at, source || ' vote_flag', vote_flag_mismatch FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND vote_flag_mismatch > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ended_at, source || ' duplicates', duplicates FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND duplicates > 0
UNION ALL
SELECT ended_at, source || ' unknown/untagged', unknown_tags + untagged_updates FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND unknown_tags + untagged_updates > 0
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Per filter over the range
panels.description: Everything the chain check measured, per (source, bundle, filter). Sort by missed % or extra_in_block.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT source, bundle, filter,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE block_status = 'ok') AS slots,
       COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE block_status = 'skipped') AS skipped,
       SUM(expected) AS expected, SUM(delivered) AS delivered, SUM(matched) AS matched,
       SUM(missed) AS missed,
       ROUND((SUM(missed)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(expected),0) * 100), 4) AS missed_pct,
       SUM(extra_in_block) AS extra_in_block,
       SUM(extra_not_in_block) AS extra_not_in_block
FROM filter_slot_checks
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
GROUP BY 1, 2, 3 ORDER BY missed_pct DESC NULLS LAST, 1, 2, 3

panels.title: Violations — example transactions
panels.description: Up to 25 examples per (window, filter, kind); the counters elsewhere are exact. reason says which clause the filter used or failed, and whether a key came from a lookup table.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts, source, bundle, filter, slot, violation, signature, reason
FROM filter_violations
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT 300

panels.title: Filter audit — Rotation and ground truth
Recent windows
panels.description: One row per subscription window. end_reason other than 'rotated' is a stream or connect error.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT started_at, source, bundle, ROUND(duration_secs::numeric, 1) AS secs, end_reason,
       delivered, slots_checked AS slots, slots_skipped AS skipped, slots_unchecked AS unchecked,
       expected, missed, extra_in_block, extra_not_in_block,
       tag_false_positive AS tag_fp, tag_missing, vote_flag_mismatch AS vote_flag,
       ROUND(connect_ms::numeric, 0) AS connect_ms, ROUND(first_msg_ms::numeric, 0) AS first_msg_ms,
       ROUND((vs_shred_p50_us / 1000)::numeric, 2) AS vs_shred_p50_ms
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 200

panels.title: Window errors
panels.description: Windows per 10 minutes that ended in an error instead of rotating.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ended_at, '10m'), source AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND end_reason LIKE 'error%'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Connect and first message
panels.description: Per window: connect + subscribe, and time to the first message of any kind.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ended_at AS time, source || ' connect' AS metric, connect_ms AS value FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND connect_ms IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT ended_at, source || ' first msg', first_msg_ms FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND first_msg_ms IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: getBlock health
panels.description: Every getBlock the filter audit made, by status per 5 minutes. No 'ok' means no ground truth: nothing else on this dashboard is being checked.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ts, '5m'), status AS metric, COUNT(*) AS value
FROM rpc_block_fetches
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host'
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: getBlock latency
panels.description: Per call, successful fetches only.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ts AS time, rpc AS metric, latency_ms AS value
FROM rpc_block_fetches
WHERE $__timeFilter(ts) AND host = '$host' AND status = 'ok'
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Deliveries per second per window
panels.description: delivered / duration, per window and bundle — a filter that suddenly delivers far less (or nothing) shows here before it shows as misses.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT ended_at AS time, source || ' / ' || bundle AS metric, delivered / NULLIF(duration_secs, 0) AS value
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Filter audit — Latency — per window, against the shred providers and the other sources
vs fastest shred provider — p50
panels.description: Per window: this feed's arrival minus the earliest shred provider's for the same transaction. Negative = the feed was ahead of every shred provider. Needs shred providers in the config.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ended_at, '5m'), source AS metric, AVG(vs_shred_p50_us) / 1000 AS value
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND vs_shred_p50_us IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: vs fastest shred provider — p90
panels.description: Same as p50, 90th percentile per window, averaged per 5 minutes.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ended_at, '5m'), source AS metric, AVG(vs_shred_p90_us) / 1000 AS value
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND vs_shred_p90_us IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Behind the earliest source — p50 / p90
panels.description: Per window, over transactions at least two sources delivered: how far behind the first arrival from ANY source.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ended_at, '5m'), source || ' p50' AS metric, AVG(behind_p50_us) / 1000 AS value
FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND behind_p50_us IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2
UNION ALL
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ended_at, '5m'), source || ' p90', AVG(behind_p90_us) / 1000
FROM filter_windows WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND behind_p90_us IS NOT NULL GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Winrate
panels.description: Share of contested transactions this feed delivered first, per 5 minutes.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ended_at, '5m'), source AS metric, SUM(wins)::float / NULLIF(SUM(contested),0) * 100 AS value
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Server delay — receive minus created_at, p50
panels.description: Our receive time minus the server's created_at timestamp. Crosses two clocks, so it includes the skew between them: watch the trend, not the level.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroupAlias(ended_at, '5m'), source AS metric, AVG(server_delay_p50_us) / 1000 AS value
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source) AND server_delay_p50_us IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Latency by bundle over the range
panels.description: Does a filter make delivery slower? Averages of the per-window percentiles.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT source, bundle, COUNT(*) AS windows, SUM(delivered) AS delivered,
       ROUND((AVG(vs_shred_p50_us) / 1000)::numeric, 2) AS vs_shred_p50_ms,
       ROUND((AVG(vs_shred_p90_us) / 1000)::numeric, 2) AS vs_shred_p90_ms,
       ROUND((AVG(behind_p50_us) / 1000)::numeric, 2) AS behind_p50_ms,
       ROUND((SUM(wins)::numeric / NULLIF(SUM(contested),0) * 100), 2) AS winrate_pct,
       ROUND(AVG(first_msg_ms)::numeric, 0) AS first_msg_ms
FROM filter_windows
WHERE $__timeFilter(ended_at) AND host = '$host' AND source IN ($source)
GROUP BY 1, 2 ORDER BY 1, 2
